newsitem.title: ITALY: OLYMPICS-ROME PROTESTERS SEEK MEETING WITH SAMARANCH.
newsitem.headline: OLYMPICS-ROME PROTESTERS SEEK MEETING WITH SAMARANCH.

text.p: A group opposing Rome's bid to host the 2004 Olympics said on Friday it would seek a meeting with IOC chief Juan Antonio Samaranch to explain why it feels the Games would harm the Italian capital.

Members of the Committee Against the Olympics in Rome told a news conference they would give Samaranch a dossier "with all the documented data on the lies of the project" to develop Rome for the Summer Games.
The group consists of about 100 intellectuals and environmentalists who say the Games would be costly, disruptive and environmentally harmful to the city, which last hosted the Games in 1960.
Promoters of Rome's candidacy have promised that Rome would undergo a major facelift to be ready for the Olympics.
German anti-Olympic protesters severely disrupted Berlin's campaign to host the 2000 Games, which eventually went to Sydney, and the Italians will no doubt hope for similar success.
The other candidates are Cape Town, Athens, St Petersburg, Lille, Stockholm, Rio de Janeiro, San Juan, Buenos Aires, Seville and Istanbul.
The IOC will announce the winning city in September this year.
